deductions: Continuity: The opener says to “discuss relevant cellular, satellite and edge options,” while section 02 limits capability discussion to the approved product list.
Clarity: “Peplink help” reads like a note label rather than a clear instruction to a rep.
Tightness and organisation: “Stand render supplied by MER Events. Swipe to pan on mobile” interrupts the briefing copy.
Actionability: The opener does not carry section 02’s approved-list condition into its instruction to discuss options.
Continuity: “Welcome channel partners” is not connected to the visitor priorities immediately above it.
Clarity: “Appropriate M2M specialist” leaves the first hand-off unclear here; section 02 supplies the route.
Tightness and organisation: “Qualified, owned follow-up” repeats the goal without adding a concrete measure.
Actionability: “Peter: set the event targets” names the owner but leaves the proposed target decision unspecified.
Continuity: The approved-product-list rule under “Explain the stand line” conflicts with the broader options instruction in section 00.
Clarity: “Approved event product list” has no named place for a rep to check it.
Tightness and organisation: The three audience prompts repeat the same “ask what an outage interrupts” pattern.
Actionability: “Ask a specialist to explain any requested capability” gives no fallback if the specialist cannot confirm an approved claim.
Continuity: “Use the lead-capture procedure” relies on the reader finding section 04; a direct section reference would make the hand-off clearer.
Clarity: “Appropriate M2M Zoho CRM” does not tell a rep what determines the destination.
Tightness and organisation: The “After the event” paragraph combines debrief escalation, CRM assignment and salesperson follow-up in one dense block.
Actionability: “Flag any time-sensitive promise” does not say how the debrief owner will identify it in the submitted record.
Continuity: “Cameron Walsh is the stand contact for operational issues” appears after the failed-scan procedure without saying when to involve Cameron.
Clarity: “The event code from your sales manager” does not identify which manager supplies it.
Tightness and organisation: “Press SUBMIT” appears in both “The save rule” and “At the stand”; the repetition is useful but occupies two instruction blocks.
Actionability: The failed-scan path says to give notes to Peter or Eerin that day, but gives no immediate step if neither is available before the visitor leaves.

overall_findings: Sections 00 and 02 need one consistent rule for discussing cellular, satellite and edge options before the event product list is approved.
No supplied section names a customer or project, gives an unapproved count or outcome, or contradicts the stated confidentiality boundary. Section 04 retains the SUBMIT instruction.
Section 05 was not supplied, so preservation of its live roster and event timetable cannot be verified in this pass.
